# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Mohamed_2026_tacrolimus"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Mohamed_2026_tacrolimus"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-026-04152-x> (open access, CC BY 4.0, PMC13642457)

Mohamed et al. modelled routine tacrolimus therapeutic-drug-monitoring
concentrations from 44 adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT)
recipients to ask whether the gut microbiome explains part of the
between-patient variability in tacrolimus clearance (CL) and oral
bioavailability (F). Every concentration was at steady state: average
concentrations during the continuous IV infusion given from day -3, and
troughs after the switch to oral immediate-release capsules. The authors did
not fit a compartmental model. Both kinds of observation were fitted
simultaneously with the steady-state infusion relations (Eqs. 1 and 2):

$$C_{av,ss} = \frac{\text{IV infusion rate}}{CL}, \qquad
C_{trough,ss} = \frac{\text{Daily dose} \times F}{CL \times 24}$$

treating the oral trough as approximately the daily average because of
tacrolimus's long half-life. F is 1 for the IV records and logit-normal for
oral records. CL carries linear factors for CYP3A5\*1 carriage, voriconazole
and eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2, and exponential effects of three stool bacterial
species; logit(F) carries additive shifts for corticosteroids, laxatives and
ten bacterial species. The bacterial covariates are centred-log-ratio (CLR)
transformed relative abundances, centred at the cohort median of each species.

The packaged model is therefore **algebraic**: no time dimension, no
compartments and no dosing events. The daily dose is supplied as the
covariate `DOSE_TAC_MGD` (mg/day; for the IV infusion, 24 x the hourly
rate), the route as `ROUTE_ORAL`, and each observation row returns the
steady-state concentration `Cc` (ng/mL).

# Population

The model was fitted to 658 steady-state whole-blood concentrations (222 IV
continuous-infusion Css and 436 oral troughs) from 44 adults enrolled in the
University of Minnesota MT2017-12 microbiome study (Mohamed 2026 Table I).
Thirty-three were 65 years or younger; 13 were female; 42 self-reported as
Caucasian and 2 as Native American; median actual body weight was 86.7 kg
(46.5-160.7). The most common diagnoses were acute myeloid leukemia (34.1%)
and myelodysplastic syndromes (29.5%). CYP3A5 genotypes were \*3/\*3 in 77.3%,
\*1/\*3 in 18.2% and \*1/\*1 in 4.5%. The median IV infusion rate was 86 ug/h
(2.064 mg/day) and the median oral dose 3 mg/day; the median IV Css was
10.85 ng/mL (3.6-20.8) and the median oral trough 8.9 ng/mL (1.5-27.5).
Voriconazole accompanied 45% of the concentrations, corticosteroids 23.9% and
laxatives 10%; eGFR was below 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2 at 14.4% (Table II). One
stool sample per patient (median day 14 after HCT) was sequenced by shotgun
metagenomics.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Mohamed_2026_tacrolimus"))$population)
```

# Source trace

The final estimates are taken from the NONMEM control stream in
Supplementary file 1 (`$THETA`, `$OMEGA`, `$SIGMA`), which carries them to
more digits than Table III and rounds to every Table III value. The
per-parameter origin is also recorded next to each `ini()` entry in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Mohamed_2026_tacrolimus.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Steady-state relations | $C = F \cdot \text{rate} / CL$ | Eqs. 1-2; control stream `CSS = F1*RATE*1e3/CL` |
| IIV on CL, logit-normal F | $CL_i = TVCL\,e^{\eta}$; $\text{logit}F_i = \text{logit}TVF + \eta$ | Eqs. 3-5 |
| Categorical effects | CL x (1 + theta); logit(F) + theta | Eqs. 7-8; control stream |
| Microbiome effects | CL x exp(theta (CLR - median)); logit(F) + theta (CLR - median) | Eqs. 9-10; control stream (medians) |
| Proportional residual error | $C(1 + \varepsilon)$ | Eq. 6 |
| `lcl` | log(6.9101) L/h | `$THETA` T1; Table III 6.91 |
| `logitfdepot` | 0.59240 (F = 0.644) | `$THETA` T2; Table III 0.644 |
| `e_cyp3a5_expr_cl` | 0.57532 | `$THETA` 3; Table III 0.575 |
| `e_conmed_voriconazole_cl` | -0.20317 | `$THETA` 4; Table III -0.203 |
| `e_renalimp_cl` | -0.16902 | `$THETA` 5; Table III -0.169 |
| `e_conmed_steroid_fdepot` | -0.44743 | `$THETA` 6; Table III -0.447 |
| `e_conmed_laxative_fdepot` | 0.52704 | `$THETA` 7; Table III 0.527 |
| `e_gut_*_clr_cl` (3 species) | 0.020259, 0.011339, -0.034464 | `$THETA` T8-T10; Table III |
| `e_gut_*_clr_fdepot` (10 species) | 0.11965 ... -0.072378 | `$THETA` T11-T20; Table III |
| CLR centring medians | -0.7839, -1.4625, -1.6278, -0.6759, -1.7002, -1.4625, -0.3043, -1.5057, -1.7002, -1.3441 | Control stream `$PRED` |
| `etalcl` | 0.026110 | `$OMEGA`; Table III 0.0261 |
| `etalogitfdepot` | 0.20796 | `$OMEGA`; Table III 0.208 |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.12228) = 0.34969 | `$SIGMA`; Table III 0.122 (CV 35%) |

# The microbiome covariates

The CLR value of a species depends on the whole panel it was computed in.
Mohamed 2026 kept the 32 of 897 species present in at least 30% of samples
with a mean relative abundance of at least 0.1%, replaced zeros by half the
smallest relative abundance, and CLR-transformed. Supplementary file 3 gives
the per-patient relative abundances of all 897 species. Applying that recipe
reproduces the control stream's centring medians only when the 32 retained
abundances are first re-closed to proportions (so that they sum to 1) before
the zero replacement; the values below were computed that way by the
maintainers. They are the CLR values of the ten model species for the 44
patients, used here as the virtual cohort's microbiome.

```{r clr-data}
  uniformis = -0.7839, ovatus = -1.4625, fermentum = -1.6278,
  lactatiformans = -0.6759, atypica = -1.7002, intestinalis = -1.4625,
  faecium = -0.3043, lenta = -1.5057, caecimuris = -1.7002,
  salivarius = -1.3441

  species = names(clr_median),
  control_stream = clr_median,
  recomputed = vapply(clr_obs[names(clr_median)], median, numeric(1))
)
# Fixed data on both sides; the remaining gap is the 4-decimal rounding of
# the control-stream medians and of the values above.
stopifnot(nrow(clr_obs) == 44, all(abs(med_chk$control_stream - med_chk$recomputed) < 0.01))
med_chk |>
  dplyr::rename("Species" = species, "Control-stream median" = control_stream, "Recomputed median" = recomputed) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, row.names = FALSE, caption = "CLR centring medians: control stream vs recomputed from Supplementary file 3.")
```

# Typical-value check against the closed form

With the random effects zeroed, the model must return Eqs. 1-2 with the
final estimates. The event table puts one observation row per scenario on a
single subject; `time` is only a row index, since the model has no time
dimension. The microbiome values are drawn from the observed patients, so the
check exercises every covariate path.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Mohamed_2026_tacrolimus")
expit <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  ROUTE_ORAL = 0:1, CYP3A5_EXPR = 0:1, CONMED_VORICONAZOLE = 0:1,
  RENALIMP = 0:1, CONMED_STEROID = 0:1, CONMED_LAXATIVE = 0:1
) |>
  mutate(DOSE_TAC_MGD = ifelse(ROUTE_ORAL == 1, 3, 2.064))
grid <- dplyr::bind_cols(grid, clr_obs[rep_len(seq_len(44), nrow(grid)), names(clr_names)])
names(grid)[match(names(clr_names), names(grid))] <- clr_names

ev_typ <- grid |> mutate(id = 1L, time = seq_len(n()), evid = 0L, amt = 0)
typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame"))
stopifnot(nrow(typ) == nrow(grid))

d <- function(sp) grid[[clr_names[[sp]]]] - clr_median[[sp]]
cl_cf <- 6.9101 * (1 + 0.57532 * grid$CYP3A5_EXPR) * (1 - 0.20317 * grid$CONMED_VORICONAZOLE) *
  (1 - 0.16902 * grid$RENALIMP) *
  exp(0.020259 * d("uniformis") + 0.011339 * d("ovatus") - 0.034464 * d("fermentum"))
logitf_cf <- 0.59240 - 0.44743 * grid$CONMED_STEROID + 0.52704 * grid$CONMED_LAXATIVE +
  0.11965 * d("lactatiformans") + 0.050486 * d("atypica") + 0.050774 * d("intestinalis") -
  0.060493 * d("faecium") - 0.067766 * d("uniformis") - 0.059150 * d("ovatus") +
  0.055190 * d("fermentum") + 0.13937 * d("lenta") - 0.11461 * d("caecimuris") -
  0.072378 * d("salivarius")
f_cf <- ifelse(grid$ROUTE_ORAL == 1, expit(logitf_cf), 1)
closed_form <- f_cf * grid$DOSE_TAC_MGD / 24 * 1000 / cl_cf

# Same parameters on both sides, so the only difference is floating point.
stopifnot(all(abs(typ$Cc / closed_form - 1) < 1e-10))

```

At the cohort-median microbiome and without interacting covariates, the
typical IV Css at the median 86 ug/h rate is
`r round(2.064 / 24 * 1000 / 6.9101, 2)` ng/mL and the typical oral trough at
3 mg/day is `r round(expit(0.5924) * 3 / 24 * 1000 / 6.9101, 2)` ng/mL
(F = `r round(expit(0.5924), 3)`).

# Replication of Figure 4

Figure 4 shows, for each bacterial species with a significant effect, the
oral steady-state trough at the 5th, 25th, 75th and 95th percentile of its
CLR value, relative to the reference trough (3 mg/day, median CLR values,
CYP3A5\*3/\*3, no interacting co-medication). Because the model is linear in
dose, the ratio is independent of the dose. The paper's points are medians of
simulations with parameter uncertainty (SIR); the typical-value ratio is
compared with the points digitised by the maintainers from the published
figure (pixel centre of each diamond).

```{r figure4}
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~species, ~pctl, ~clr, ~published,
  "lactatiformans", "95th", 4.7611, 1.208,
  "lactatiformans", "75th", 2.3639, 1.123,
  "lactatiformans", "25th", -1.7441, 0.953,
  "lactatiformans", "5th", -4.6496, 0.818,
  "fermentum", "95th", 7.8985, 1.625,
  "fermentum", "75th", 2.9291, 1.273,
  "fermentum", "25th", -4.8146, 0.836,
  "fermentum", "5th", -6.3934, 0.763,
  "lenta", "95th", 4.4791, 1.247,
  "lenta", "75th", -0.1147, 1.066,
  "lenta", "25th", -3.671, 0.889,
  "lenta", "5th", -6.0527, 0.762,
  "salivarius", "95th", 5.8271, 0.811,
  "salivarius", "75th", 2.7461, 0.894,
  "salivarius", "25th", -2.5107, 1.028,
  "salivarius", "5th", -6.1855, 1.113,
  "faecium", "95th", 12.5776, 0.709,
  "faecium", "75th", 2.3098, 0.944,
  "faecium", "25th", -3.6053, 1.067,
  "faecium", "5th", -7.2938, 1.137,
  "caecimuris", "95th", 5.0255, 0.714,
  "caecimuris", "75th", 1.0511, 0.887,
  "caecimuris", "25th", -3.6762, 1.075,
  "caecimuris", "5th", -6.6801, 1.176,
  "uniformis", "95th", 7.7783, 0.653,
  "uniformis", "75th", 4.732, 0.768,
  "uniformis", "25th", -1.8919, 1.049,
  "uniformis", "5th", -6.1855, 1.247,
  "ovatus", "95th", 7.8985, 0.718,
  "ovatus", "75th", 4.5056, 0.816,
  "ovatus", "25th", -2.1668, 1.022,
  "ovatus", "5th", -6.3934, 1.155
)

# One reference row, then one row per figure point with only that species moved.
base_cov <- as.data.frame(as.list(setNames(clr_median, clr_names)))
base_cov <- dplyr::mutate(base_cov,
  ROUTE_ORAL = 1L, DOSE_TAC_MGD = 3, CYP3A5_EXPR = 0L, CONMED_VORICONAZOLE = 0L,
  RENALIMP = 0L, CONMED_STEROID = 0L, CONMED_LAXATIVE = 0L
)
ev4 <- base_cov[rep(1, nrow(fig4) + 1), ]
for (i in seq_len(nrow(fig4))) ev4[i + 1, clr_names[[fig4$species[i]]]] <- fig4$clr[i]
ev4 <- ev4 |> mutate(id = 1L, time = seq_len(n()), evid = 0L, amt = 0)
s4 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev4, returnType = "data.frame"))
fig4$model <- s4$Cc[-1] / s4$Cc[1]
fig4$diff <- fig4$model - fig4$published
low95 <- fig4$model[fig4$pctl == "95th" & fig4$species %in% c("uniformis", "ovatus", "faecium", "caecimuris")]
stopifnot(all(low95 < 0.8), fig4$model[fig4$species == "fermentum" & fig4$pctl == "95th"] > 1.25)

# Deterministic typical values against medians of the authors' uncertainty
# simulation; a wrong sign, median or coefficient moves a point by > 0.05.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4$diff) < 0.02))

fig4 |>
  mutate(species = factor(species, levels = unique(species))) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = interaction(pctl, species, sep = " "), yend = interaction(pctl, species, sep = " "))) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.8, xmax = 1.25, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(x = published, shape = "Published (digitised)"), size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x = model, shape = "Packaged model (typical)"), size = 1.8, colour = "red") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 4), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Oral trough relative to reference", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Replicates Figure 4 of Mohamed 2026. The largest difference between the
packaged model and the published points is
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(fig4$diff)))` on the ratio scale. The model
reproduces the paper's reading that only the 95th-percentile abundance of
*L. fermentum* (`r sprintf("%.2f", fig4$model[fig4$species == "fermentum" & fig4$pctl == "95th"])`-fold) and the 95th
percentiles of *B. uniformis*, *B. ovatus*, *E. faecium* and *B. caecimuris*
(`r sprintf("%.2f", min(low95))`-`r sprintf("%.2f", max(low95))`-fold)
fall outside 0.8-1.25.

# Replication of Figure 5

Figure 5 gives the percentage change in the oral trough per one-unit increase
in each species' CLR value from its median. The bar heights below were
digitised by the maintainers from the figure (90 pixels per percentage
point).

```{r figure5}
fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~species, ~published,
  "fermentum", 5.58,
  "lenta", 4.79,
  "lactatiformans", 4.26,
  "faecium", -2.12,
  "salivarius", -2.49,
  "ovatus", -3.12,
  "caecimuris", -4.01,
  "uniformis", -4.38
)
ev5 <- base_cov[rep(1, nrow(fig5) + 1), ]
for (i in seq_len(nrow(fig5))) {
  ev5[i + 1, clr_names[[fig5$species[i]]]] <- clr_median[[fig5$species[i]]] + 1
}
ev5 <- ev5 |> mutate(id = 1L, time = seq_len(n()), evid = 0L, amt = 0)
s5 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev5, returnType = "data.frame"))
fig5$model <- 100 * (s5$Cc[-1] / s5$Cc[1] - 1)

# The published bars are medians over parameter uncertainty, a few hundredths
# of a percentage point to ~0.1 away from the point-estimate value.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig5$model - fig5$published) < 0.25))

fig5 |>
  dplyr::rename("Species" = species, "Published (%)" = published, "Packaged model (%)" = model) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Percent change in the oral trough per unit CLR increase (Figure 5).")
```

# Virtual cohort against the observed concentrations

A stochastic simulation with random effects and residual error, for 200
virtual patients per route at the median doses (86 ug/h IV, 3 mg/day oral).
The microbiome profiles are resampled whole from the 44 patients, preserving
the correlation between species. CYP3A5\*1 carriage (22.7%) and the
per-concentration frequencies of voriconazole, eGFR < 60, corticosteroids and
laxatives (Tables I-II) are drawn independently.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_arm <- 200
make_arm <- function(route, dose) {
  prof <- clr_obs[sample.int(44, n_arm, replace = TRUE), names(clr_names)]
  names(prof) <- clr_names
  data.frame(
    ROUTE_ORAL = route, DOSE_TAC_MGD = dose,
    CYP3A5_EXPR = rbinom(n_arm, 1, 10 / 44),
    CONMED_VORICONAZOLE = rbinom(n_arm, 1, 0.4498),
    RENALIMP = rbinom(n_arm, 1, 0.1444),
    CONMED_STEROID = rbinom(n_arm, 1, 0.2386),
    CONMED_LAXATIVE = rbinom(n_arm, 1, 0.1003)
  ) |> dplyr::bind_cols(prof)
}
set.seed(2026)
cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(make_arm(0L, 2.064), make_arm(1L, 3)) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()), time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = 0)
sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = cohort, returnType = "data.frame"))
sim$route <- ifelse(cohort$ROUTE_ORAL[sim$id] == 1, "Oral trough (3 mg/day)", "IV Css (86 ug/h)")

obs <- data.frame(
  route = c("IV Css (86 ug/h)", "Oral trough (3 mg/day)"),
  obs_median = c(10.85, 8.9), obs_lo = c(3.6, 1.5), obs_hi = c(20.8, 27.5)
)
cmp <- sim |>
  group_by(route) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(sim), sim_p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), sim_p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95)) |>
  left_join(obs, by = "route")

# The observed doses were titrated to targets, so the observed median at the
# median dose is only a structural anchor: a unit (x1000) or route-F error
# moves the median by far more than this bound.
stopifnot(all(cmp$sim_median / cmp$obs_median > 0.67 & cmp$sim_median / cmp$obs_median < 1.5))

cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Route" = route, "Simulated median" = sim_median, "Simulated 5th pct" = sim_p05,
    "Simulated 95th pct" = sim_p95, "Observed median" = obs_median,
    "Observed min" = obs_lo, "Observed max" = obs_hi
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated steady-state concentrations (ng/mL) vs Table I.")

ggplot(sim, aes(x = route, y = sim)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = obs, aes(y = obs_median), colour = "red", size = 3, shape = 18) +
  geom_errorbar(data = obs, aes(y = obs_median, ymin = obs_lo, ymax = obs_hi), colour = "red", width = 0.15) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Steady-state tacrolimus (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Red diamonds and bars are the observed median and range from Table I. At the
median doses the simulated medians are
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (cmp$sim_median[1] / cmp$obs_median[1] - 1))` (IV) and
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (cmp$sim_median[2] / cmp$obs_median[2] - 1))` (oral)
above the observed medians, and the simulated 5th-95th percentiles span most of
the observed ranges. An exact match is not expected: the doses were titrated
to trough targets (12-15 ng/mL in week 1, then 5-10 ng/mL), so patients with
high concentrations had their doses lowered, and the observed median
concentration does not correspond to a fixed median dose.

# Why no PKNCA section

The model has no time dimension. It returns a single steady-state
concentration for a given daily dose, route and covariate set, so there is no
concentration-time profile for a non-compartmental analysis, and the paper
reports no NCA parameters. The model is validated against its closed form,
against the paper's covariate simulations (Figures 4 and 5) and against the
observed concentration summary (Table I).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Algebraic encoding.** The paper's model is Eqs. 1-2 themselves; it
  estimates no volume of distribution or absorption rate, and none is
  invented here. The model returns steady-state concentrations only.
* **Dose as a covariate.** The control stream reads an hourly `RATE` (mg/h;
  the oral daily dose divided by 24 for oral records) and computes
  `CSS = F1 * RATE * 1e3 / CL`. The packaged model takes the daily amount,
  `DOSE_TAC_MGD` = 24 x `RATE`, and returns ng/mL. For an IV infusion it is
  24 x the infusion rate (86 ug/h -> 2.064 mg/day, as stated in the Results).
* **Oral trough as daily average.** As in the paper, the oral prediction is
  the average steady-state concentration; the actual trough of twice-daily
  dosing is slightly lower. This is part of the published model, not a
  packaging choice.
* **Final estimates from the control stream.** Table III prints the
  estimates to three significant figures; the control stream in
  Supplementary file 1 carries the same estimates to five, and those are used.
  Typical F is the inverse logit of `$THETA` 2 (0.59240 -> 0.6439, Table III
  0.644).
* **IIV and residual error.** `$OMEGA` holds the variances (0.026110 on log
  CL, 0.20796 on logit F); the CL-F covariance in the base model was removed
  before the final model (Methods), so the IIV is diagonal. `$SIGMA` holds the
  proportional variance 0.12228, so `propSd` = 0.34969. The IIV on logit F
  applies to oral records only; IV records have F = 1, as in the control
  stream.
* **CYP3A5 orientation.** The control-stream column `CYP3A5_3_2` is 1 for
  \*3/\*3 (factor 1) and 0 for \*1 carriers (factor 1 + 0.575), so
  `CYP3A5_EXPR = 1 - CYP3A5_3_2`.
* **eGFR category.** The eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2 group (2021 CKD-EPI
  race-free equation) is carried as `RENALIMP`, with that threshold documented
  in the covariate notes.
* **Microbiome covariates.** The CLR values must be computed the way the
  paper computed them, over the same 32-species panel (see "The microbiome
  covariates"); a CLR value from a different panel or pipeline is not
  comparable. The re-closure of the 32 retained abundances before zero
  replacement is inferred from the control-stream medians, which it
  reproduces to within 0.006; the Methods do not state it. Bacteroides
  ovatus (CL), Veillonella atypica and Sellimonas intestinalis (F) have 95% CIs
  that include zero but were kept in the final model by the authors and are
  kept here.
* **Figure 4 percentiles.** The CLR percentiles printed on Figure 4 differ
  slightly from the 44-patient percentiles of the recomputed values above
  (probably because they were taken over the 658 concentration records); the
  printed values are used for the replication.
* **Screened covariates.** Age > 65 years, body weight, ideal body weight,
  sex, conditioning regimen, HLA match, POR\*28, CYP3A4\*1B, ABCB1 1236C>T,
  posaconazole, fluconazole, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, dihydropyridine
  calcium-channel blockers, bilirubin, haemoglobin, haematocrit, blood urea
  nitrogen, albumin and microbiome alpha diversity were screened and not
  retained. Several are listed in `covariatesDataExcluded` for provenance.
* **Errata.** No correction notice was found for this article in Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-11-18).
